name: Imran Cafeteria
why_it_matters: The original BBQ-street kebab shop at Khayam Chowk — started by Muhammad Yusuf, now run by his grandson Abdul Hameed (some sources say son Zeeshan). Coal-fired tujj (marinated mutton skewers) served with six chutneys and lavasa. Roughly 50 years on the same corner; the shop most travel writers point to when they say 'Khayam Chowk'.
insider_tip: Come after 7pm — the grills only fire up in the evening, and the best skewers move fast. Sit on the bench outside; the tin-roofed interior fills up with smoke.
signature_address: BBQ Street, Bishember Nagar, Khayam Chowk, Srinagar 190003

name: Sher Barbeque Cafeteria
why_it_matters: Reportedly around 80 years old — among the oldest skewer shops on the chowk. Lean mutton marinated in yoghurt, edible oil and spice, charcoal-roasted, served with assorted chutneys and free lavasa. The Khaleej Times profile of 'Sher Khan's skewer shop' refers to this stall.
insider_tip: Order by the dozen; portions are calibrated for that. The chutneys (mint, walnut, tomato) are part of the experience — don't skip them.

name: Shahi Darbar
why_it_matters: The Khayam Chowk stall locals send you to for fried fish and fish kebabs rather than mutton. Tandoori rotis paired with mutton keema curry or chicken korma; portions and prices both wholesome. Less famous than Imran/Sher, which is why the queue is shorter.
insider_tip: Skip the kebabs (Imran does them better) — order the fish kebabs and a stack of tandoori rotis with mutton keema.
signature_address: Khayam Chowk, Opposite SMD School, Srinagar 190001

name: Gareeb Nawaz
why_it_matters: Run by Mustafa, a 40+ year veteran of the tujji craft — said to have opened around the same time Khayam Cinema (now Khyber Hospital) did. One of the founding stalls of the BBQ street, with a quieter corner spot than Imran.
insider_tip: Watch the marinated meat being threaded onto skewers and grilled — Mustafa salts and bastes constantly. Ten skewers + lavasa is the standard order.

name: Khaak Saar Harissa
why_it_matters: A half-century-old harissa shop in Rajouri Kadal run by Muhammad Ashraf, named after the family's old Lal Chowk hotel. Mutton slow-cooked overnight in earthen pots with fennel, cinnamon, cardamom and fried Kashmiri shallots; sealed with mustard oil. Open only in winter (December–March).
insider_tip: Arrive between 6 and 8am — Ashraf starts cooking at 4am after morning prayers and the pots empty by mid-morning. Order it topped with a fried mutton kebab.

name: Aali Kadal Harissa (Bhat family)
why_it_matters: Reportedly ~200 years old, currently run by Ghulam Mohammad (in his 80s) and his son Zahoor Ahmad Bhat — the fourth/fifth generation behind a stove in old Srinagar. Featured by Better India and Goya. Customers book orders days in advance during peak winter; Dilip Kumar is among names the family cites.
insider_tip: It's a tiny rust-coloured wooden storefront with no signage near the kadal — ask any local for the 'purana harissa shop'. Get there by 7am or it's gone.

name: Bat Kandur
why_it_matters: A 200-year-old kandur (clay-tandoor neighbourhood bakery) in Batiyar, Aali Kadal — set up when the area still had ~600 Pandit families and 29 Muslim families. The structure is unaltered; multiple bakers have run it but the recipes haven't changed. A symbol of pre-1990 syncretic downtown Srinagar.
insider_tip: Open only at sunrise through mid-morning (~5:30–10:30am). Buy a girda or tsot warm and walk to a tea stall for noon chai — the standard Kashmiri breakfast.

name: Ahad Sons
why_it_matters: Founded in the late 1970s by Wazwan chef Abdul Ahad Khan (the family is named in Roli Books' 'Wazwan' monograph). For three decades the Ahad Sons kitchen has catered Indian Presidents, PMs, CMs, film stars and Kashmiri weddings. The Fateh Kadal address is the working kitchen, not a walk-in restaurant — order in advance.
insider_tip: This isn't a sit-down spot — it's a wedding-grade catering kitchen. Phone ahead a day before for a takeaway traz; eat it at your hotel with naan and lavasa from a nearby kandur.
signature_address: Narparistan, New Fateh Kadal, near J&K Bank, Fateh Kadal, Srinagar 190002

name: Al Lazzez Harisa
why_it_matters: A working harissa shop on Harisa Chowk, Khanyar — listed on Swiggy and Justdial, which means it's one of the few traditional outlets that has gone semi-digital while keeping the dawn-cook routine. Smaller than the Aali Kadal/Rajouri Kadal landmarks but on the same kadal-belt circuit.
insider_tip: Order through the door before 9am or use Swiggy in the dead of winter (Dec–Feb only). They also sell harissa by weight to take home — 250g feeds two with lavasa.
